paragraphs.title: The Psalm’s Heading and Plea for Rescue

easy.explanation: The heading says, “To the chief Musician, upon Jonath el em rechokim, Michtam of David.”
easy.q: To whom is the psalm attributed in the heading?

easy.explanation: The heading refers to the time “when the Philistines took him in Gath.”
easy.q: Where did the Philistines seize David?

easy.explanation: He begins, “Be merciful unto me, O God.”
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist appeal for mercy?

answers: Because enemies are pressing him continually
Because he wants to leave the city
Because he wants to praise the Philistines
medium.explanation: He says that man would swallow him up and that he is oppressed daily.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask God for mercy and help?

medium.explanation: The expression describes enemies seeking to overpower or destroy him.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “swallow me up” mean in this context?

answers: The danger lasted only a moment
The danger happened only at night
medium.explanation: The word “daily” emphasizes the continuing nature of the oppression.
medium.q: What does the repeated idea of being attacked “daily” show?

answers: David’s seizure, continual oppression, and a plea to God
challenge.explanation: The heading gives the setting, and the verses describe oppression and a prayer for mercy.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the opening of the psalm?

answers: The many enemies lead him to seek God’s help
The enemies cause him to stop speaking
The enemies cause him to praise them
challenge.explanation: Because many fight against him, he turns to God for protection.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the many enemies and the psalmist’s prayer?

answers: The psalmist’s distress and appeal to God
challenge.explanation: The opening centers on his oppression and his request for divine mercy.
challenge.q: What is the main focus of these verses?

short_answers.question: What is the name of the city mentioned in the psalm’s heading?
short_answers.explanation: The heading says that the Philistines took David in Gath.

easy.explanation: He says, “What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist do when he is afraid?

easy.explanation: He says, “In God I will praise his word.”
He says, “I will not fear what flesh can do unto me.”
easy.q: Whom does the psalmist refuse to fear after trusting God?

medium.explanation: His trust in God gives him confidence despite his fear.
medium.q: What brings the psalmist from fear to confidence?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that he has placed his confidence in God.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “I have put my trust” mean?

answers: There are no enemies in the world
He is stronger than every man
medium.explanation: His confidence in God is greater than his fear of human power.
medium.q: Why is the psalmist not afraid of what man can do?

challenge.explanation: The psalmist acknowledges fear but responds by trusting God.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in these verses?

challenge.explanation: The verse shows that trust in God is his response to fear.
challenge.q: What does the order “What time I am afraid” followed by “I will trust in thee” suggest?

answers: Human power cannot ultimately terrify one who trusts God
Human beings can save the psalmist
challenge.explanation: The psalmist places human ability beneath the security found in God.
challenge.q: What does “what flesh can do unto me” mean in context?

paragraphs.title: The Enemies’ Ambush and Judgment on Wickedness

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “Every day they wrest my words.”
easy.q: What do the enemies do with the psalmist’s words?

answers: They hide themselves and mark his steps
They invite him to a feast
easy.explanation: They gather together, hide themselves, and watch his steps while waiting for his soul.
easy.q: What do the enemies do in order to harm him?

easy.explanation: He asks God to cast down the people in His anger because of iniquity.
easy.q: What does the psalmist connect with the downfall of the wicked?

answers: They distort his words and then plot and watch against him
They praise him and then depart
medium.explanation: They wrest his words, think evil against him, and lie in wait for his soul.
medium.q: How are the enemies’ words related to their actions?

answers: They follow or watch where he goes
medium.explanation: The phrase describes careful observation and pursuit.
medium.q: What does “they mark my steps” mean?

answers: Iniquity is a reason for God to cast down the wicked
Iniquity causes him to thank the enemies
Iniquity makes him join the enemies
medium.explanation: He asks whether they should escape by iniquity and calls on God to cast them down.
medium.q: What connection does the psalmist make between iniquity and judgment?

answers: They distort his words, think evil, hide, and watch his steps
They forget him and leave the place
challenge.explanation: The verses present a series of hostile actions against the psalmist.
challenge.q: Which description best presents the continuing threat from the enemies?

answers: The enemies plot against him, while God judges wickedness
The enemies rescue him, while God lies in wait
The enemies praise God, while God hides His word
challenge.explanation: The enemies act wickedly, and the psalmist asks God to judge them.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the enemies’ action and the action requested of God?

answers: That the wicked should be exalted
That the wicked should be brought low
That the wicked should mark his steps
challenge.explanation: To cast down means to humble or overthrow them.
challenge.q: What does the request “cast down the people” express?

paragraphs.title: Preserved Tears and Confidence in God’s Help

easy.explanation: He says, “Put thou my tears into thy bottle.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to put into His bottle?

easy.explanation: He says, “Then shall mine enemies turn back.”
easy.q: What will happen to the enemies when the psalmist cries unto God?

easy.explanation: He declares, “This I know; for God is for me.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist know about God?

answers: His travels and times of distress
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks God to remember the difficult times through which he has wandered.
medium.q: What does “my wanderings” refer to in context?

answers: God is asked to collect and preserve the psalmist’s tears
The bottle is to be poured on the enemies
The psalmist wants to hide his tears from God
medium.explanation: The bottle symbolizes God’s remembrance and care for his suffering.
medium.q: How are the tears and the bottle related?

medium.explanation: He says, “In God I will praise his word,” and again praises His word in the LORD.
medium.q: What does the psalmist repeatedly praise in verses 10–11?

answers: Wandering and tears, God’s help, the retreat of enemies, and trust
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from remembered suffering to confidence that God helps and protects him.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes these verses?

answers: God’s support makes human opposition less fearful
God’s support makes the enemies stronger
God’s support causes the psalmist to hide
challenge.explanation: Because God is for him, he says, “I will not be afraid what man can do unto me.”
challenge.q: What is the relationship between God’s being “for me” and the psalmist’s lack of fear?

answers: The reliability and importance of God’s word
The psalmist’s desire to conceal God’s word
challenge.explanation: Repeated praise shows the psalmist’s confidence in God’s declared word.
challenge.q: What does the repeated praise of God’s word emphasize?

paragraphs.title: Vows of Thanksgiving and the Light of Life

easy.explanation: He says, “Thy vows are upon me, O God: I will render praises unto thee.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist promise to do with his vows?

easy.explanation: He says, “Thou hast delivered my soul from death.”
easy.q: From what has God delivered the psalmist’s soul?

easy.explanation: He asks, “Wilt not thou deliver my feet from falling?”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to keep his feet from?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that he will give or offer praises to God.
medium.q: What does “I will render praises” mean?

answers: God has saved him from death and preserved him from stumbling
He wants to leave God’s presence
He is describing a military victory only
medium.explanation: God delivers his soul and keeps his feet from falling.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist mention both his soul and his feet?

medium.explanation: He asks to be kept from falling so that he may walk before God.
medium.q: What does the psalmist intend to do after being preserved?

answers: Deliverance from death, thanksgiving, preservation, and walking before God
challenge.explanation: The verses move from God’s deliverance to praise and continued faithful living.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the conclusion of the psalm?

answers: God’s deliverance enables the psalmist to continue walking faithfully before Him
Deliverance keeps the psalmist away from God
Deliverance causes the psalmist to hide
challenge.explanation: God saves him so that he may continue walking before God.
challenge.q: What is the connection between deliverance from death and keeping the feet from falling?

answers: Life lived before God after deliverance
Return to the darkness of the enemies
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes continued life and fellowship before God.
challenge.q: What does “the light of the living” suggest in this context?

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist promise to render unto God?
short_answers.explanation: He says, “I will render praises unto thee.”

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist ask God to deliver his feet from?
short_answers.explanation: He asks God to deliver his feet from falling so that he may walk before God.
